_headline: THE LEFTWARD CIRCUIT COMPLETES AND EXITS ON PLANE A. Invariant (a) satisfied for the first time. One new blocker found on the eastern approach.

drive_1_rightward_control.verdict: HOLDS. Unchanged by the arc fit.

drive_2_leftward_circuit.start: x1200 placed, settles x1160 y554 angle $FA (the right foot), plane A, gsp -$600 sustained held left

drive_2_leftward_circuit.verdict: COMPLETES. Rides the left arc on plane A where it is solid, crests at y426, descends and exits grounded on plane A. This is invariant (a) satisfied leftward — the first time tonight any leftward run has done anything but run flat.

drive_3_outer_face.status: NOT RUN — needs disambiguation, see below
drive_3_outer_face.why: the ruling asks for 'a drive from the west against the outer left face that must not climb it'. But the rightward control IS a westward approach at ground level and it climbs to y430 BY DESIGN — that is the intended entry. So 'from the west against the outer face' must mean a different approach than the one already passing, and I am not going to invent which one and then report a pass against my own invention.

NEW_FINDING_eastern_approach_blocked.what: from a grounded start at x1350 with gsp -$600 held, the player STOPS at x1258 (col 157), gsp 0, x_vel -12, y 557 constant. He never reaches the loop.
NEW_FINDING_eastern_approach_blocked.why_it_matters: the SAME start reached x1074 and climbed to y454 on the previous build (ac1f921a, ramp only). This is new since the left-arc fit.
NEW_FINDING_eastern_approach_blocked.why_it_is_odd: the fit touched cols 130-133. Col 157 is untouched by it. The candidate I have not verified is the content-addressed attr set renumbering, which regenerated angles/solidity/heightmaps wholesale.
NEW_FINDING_eastern_approach_blocked._not_diagnosed: I am reporting this as a measured regression candidate, not diagnosing it. It could also be that the x1350 approach never worked the way I remember and the earlier run differed in a way I have not isolated — that possibility has been the correct answer three times tonight.
